title: Nonzero discrete derivative criterion
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $i$ be a coordinate of the $n$-dimensional sign cube, and let $f$ be a real-valued function on that cube. For every point $x$ of the cube, the discrete derivative of $f$ in coordinate $i$ at $x$ is nonzero if and only if the values of $f$ at the two points obtained from $x$ by setting coordinate $i$ to $1$ and to $-1$ are unequal.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a real-valued function on the sign cube
$x$ is a point of the sign cube
